title: Harmonic Accent Token Synthesis and Component Fallbacks for Dark Themes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Create a deterministic synthesis strategy for accent tokens in dark themes that preserves brand intent, improves perceived contrast for components (buttons, tables, charts), and reduces the need for bespoke overrides. Deliver a component fallback matrix and migration guidance for existing token consumers.

Scope: token synthesis rules for surface/elevation/ink/accent; component override table for primary CTA, secondary/tertiary buttons, table row states, chart legends and axes; accessibility checks for AA/AAA where reasonable; change rollout plan for Console. Does NOT include runtime shader changes or backend routing — this is design + token mapping + dev migration notes.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a small set of meta tokens: accentBlendStrength, accentHueShift, neutralOverlayOpacity by elevation. These are algorithmic knobs used to synthesize per-component accent variants instead of shipping dozens of static tokens.
- Use perceptual color transforms (Lch chroma/alpha blending) so accent overlays maintain hue while avoiding out-of-gamut pushes (we use Lch clamp + preserve L).
- Elevation mapping: map console elevation levels (surface-0..surface-4) to overlay opacity [0%, 6%, 12%, 20%, 28%] as a default; allow per-brand overrides for stronger or subtler blends.
- Component fallbacks: a prioritized matrix so if synthesized accent yields insufficient contrast for a given component, the renderer picks a fallback from a small curated set (accent-on-dark, accent-outline, accent-soft-fill).

Why this approach: reduces token explosion across brands and densities, centralizes behavior to a reproducible algorithm, and allows runtime teams to expose a small number of user-configurable knobs (brandAccent, brandStrength) rather than many static tokens. It aligns with Redwood's goal of predictable unit economics for runtime (smaller token surface = less config/state).

Acceptance criteria:
- Design tokens RFC published and linked, with worked examples for three brand profiles (neutral, saturated, muted).
- Figma components updated to use synthesized token variables and a toggle to preview synthesized vs. static tokens.
- Engineering PR with token-to-css/ts mapping and a reference JS implementation of the synthesis function (unit tests included).
- Accessibility report with contrast ratios for: primary button (normal + disabled), table header vs body, chart legend text and markers. All must meet AA for normal text; critical CTAs should approach AAA where feasible.
- Migration guide with codemod suggestions for replacing old tokens and a rollback plan.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Synthesis adds a small runtime cost if computed in-browser; prefer build-time generation for hosted Console. For Private/on-prem we provide both generated static token bundles and a tiny synthesis runtime (<= 1 KB gz).
- Per-brand overrides will be limited to 10 values to avoid combinatorial explosion; larger brand teams can request custom token bundles.
- Exact Lch math may differ slightly between platforms (browser vs. native). We will include platform tests and a reference implementation to minimize drift.
